findings.title: Shared SSLContext accumulates client certs across all verify=True requests
findings.why_it_matters: With verify=True and cert=(cert, key), urllib3's ssl_wrap_socket calls context.load_cert_chain() on the module-level _preloaded_ssl_context. That context is now shared by every verify=True connection in the process, so the client certificate stays loaded and is presented on later TLS handshakes by unrelated Sessions and hosts that passed no cert. It also leaks one user's identity into another's requests and makes concurrent requests with different client certs race on the same context. Before the change each pool built its own context, so client certs stayed scoped to their own pool. Reproduced: request 1 with cert=('c.pem','k.pem'), then a fresh Session with no cert; the server saw a client certificate on both.
findings.suggested_fix: Only pass the shared preloaded context when no client cert is configured (client_cert is None). Otherwise leave ssl_context unset so urllib3 builds a per-pool context. In that case, set pool_kwargs['ca_certs'] to the default bundle path, or copy the preloaded context per pool. Add a regression test that sends a request with cert= and then one without cert=, and asserts that the second handshake presents no client cert.
evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:101-107 -- pool_kwargs["cert_file"] = client_cert[0]; pool_kwargs["key_file"] = client_cert[1] (set in the same pool_kwargs as the shared ssl_context)
urllib3/util/ssl_.py:429-433 -- if certfile: ... context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile) (mutates the passed-in ssl_context)
Empirical repro with local TLS server (CERT_OPTIONAL): s1.get(url, cert=(c,k)) -> client cert presented True; fresh Session s2.get(url) with no cert -> client cert presented True

residual_risks: _preloaded_ssl_context is built at import time of requests.adapters. If the certifi bundle is missing or unreadable (frozen or stripped installs), 'import requests' now fails for every user, including verify=False or custom-bundle users. Before, the 'Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle' OSError was raised lazily and only for verify=True requests.

Runtime changes to requests.utils.DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH, certs.where or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE handling that relied on the lazy per-request lookup no longer take effect for verify=True. The bundle is frozen at import time. REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is still honored because Session turns it into a str verify.
testing_gaps: No test covers cert=(cert, key) with verify=True followed by a request without cert on the shared context.
